findings.issue_text: P1: Reordering Init so search index build runs before watcher start loses events occurring during index build, leaving search permanently stale for those writes (server.go:300-308)
P1: Init failures are no longer surfaced to callers and never retried; after a transient init failure at construction, server is stuck unhealthy with no recovery path (server.go:446+)
P1: Request methods (Read, List, Create, Watch, Search, ...) no longer check initErr, so after failed init they silently proceed against an uninitialized server and return wrong/empty results
P1: Removal of cacheMu.Lock() around BuildIndex allows concurrent builds for the same key to race on the same index directory, potentially corrupting the index (bleve.go:85-99)
P2: Integration test skipped on postgres ('TODO - fix this test') masks CI coverage of exactly the init/watch ordering behavior being changed (module_server_test.go:32)
P3: Init logging of TotalDocs may conflate build output with concurrently processed events, reporting against the wrong index state (search.go:213)

Cache-stampede on BuildIndex: cacheMu lock no longer held during build, so concurrent cache misses for the same NamespacedResource each run a full bleve build (N× CPU, memory, disk I/O; N−1 built indexes discarded, leaking memory or leaving orphaned file-based directories)
Concurrent bleve.New(dir, ...) calls on the same directory path can fail or corrupt the on-disk index

P1: Lazy Init removed — NewResourceServer now calls Init synchronously, changing error contract to constructor error and blocking startup, with no tests verifying failing-init rejection, previously-lazy paths, or alternate construction paths skipping init

P2: Integration test TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer silently skipped for postgres with a 'works locally' TODO, removing coverage for a major backend in a lifecycle-changing PR
P2: Narrowed mutex scope in bleveBackend.BuildIndex allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key racing to write cache and clobbering the same directory, with no concurrency test
P2: Init ordering change (search.init before initWatcher) untested — no test asserts no events are handled before index build or that events during build aren't lost
P3: Tracer.Start calls changed from dropping ctx to propagating it (child spans now inherit context), but no test verifies span parentage to prevent regression

P1: Event-loss window — moving initWatcher() after search.init() means events written between the snapshot RV and watcher start can be missed, leaving a silently stale search index (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~300-308)

P2: Shrinking the cacheMu critical section in BuildIndex allows concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory, causing spurious errors or divergent index instances (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:~85-138)
P2: Nil-pointer panic in History/Origin when search is not configured — they call s.search.History/Origin without a nil guard, unlike Search (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~922-930)

P2: Watcher/search goroutines inherit the constructor-only ctx, so if the constructor's ctx is cancelled after construction, background work silently dies with no lazy-init fallback (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~255-261)
P2: Integration test for this server is unconditionally skipped on postgres with a TODO, silently reducing CI coverage and possibly masking a real regression (pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38)

P3: Startup now blocks and fails hard on a full index build since Init moved into NewResourceServer, converting degraded-but-working startup into hard failure for large installs (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-261)

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Reordering Init so search index build runs before watcher start loses events occurring during index build, leaving search permanently stale for those writes (server.go:300-308)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does reorder initialization in `server.Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (moved from before to after). If the watcher is responsible for catching write events to keep the search index up to date, this creates a startup window where changes occurring during index build would not be observed. However, the diff alone does not show the watcher’s semantics (e.g., whether it resumes from a resource version captured by `search.init`, or whether writes are possible before `NewResourceServer` returns since `Init` is now called during construction), so the claim of a definite, permanent staleness bug is not fully verifiable from the provided hunks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Init failures are no longer surfaced to callers and never retried; after a transient init failure at construction, server is stuck unhealthy with no recovery path (server.go:446+)

adjudication.rationale: The diff moves initialization from per-RPC methods (Create/Update/Delete/etc. previously called `s.Init(ctx)`) to construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` if it fails. That means init failures are still surfaced (earlier, at construction) rather than being hidden. Also, retry behavior was already effectively one-shot because `Init` uses `initOnce.Do`; per-call `Init` invocations did not actually retry after a failure. The claim that the server is "stuck unhealthy" after a transient init failure at construction is not supported by the diff, since construction fails and no server is returned.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Request methods (Read, List, Create, Watch, Search, ...) no longer check initErr, so after failed init they silently proceed against an uninitialized server and return wrong/empty results

adjudication.rationale: Although per-request `s.Init(ctx)` calls were removed from methods like `Create/Read/List/Watch/Search`, the diff adds an eager initialization in `NewResourceServer`: it now calls `err := s.Init(ctx)` and returns `nil, err` if initialization fails. Also `Init` returns `s.initErr` after `initOnce.Do(...)`. Therefore a failed init will prevent the server from being constructed rather than “silently proceeding against an uninitialized server”. The finding misreads the new initialization flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Removal of cacheMu.Lock() around BuildIndex allows concurrent builds for the same key to race on the same index directory, potentially corrupting the index (bleve.go:85-99)
P2: Integration test skipped on postgres ('TODO - fix this test') masks CI coverage of exactly the init/watch ordering behavior being changed (module_server_test.go:32)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a TODO and skips the integration test when `dbType == "postgres"` (module_server_test.go), which will reduce CI coverage for postgres. While the finding’s claim that it masks coverage of the specific init/watch ordering change is not directly verifiable from this diff alone, the act of skipping the test on postgres is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern (it can hide regressions on that backend).

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Init logging of TotalDocs may conflate build output with concurrently processed events, reporting against the wrong index state (search.go:213)

adjudication.rationale: The diff only adds an info log in `searchSupport.init()` reporting `s.search.TotalDocs()` after initialization. Nothing in the shown changes demonstrates that events are concurrently processed during `init()` in a way that would make `TotalDocs` refer to a “wrong index state”. In fact, `server.Init()` now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()`, which would reduce concurrent indexing from watcher-driven events during init. Any remaining concurrency would depend on unseen code, so the claimed conflation can’t be verified from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Cache-stampede on BuildIndex: cacheMu lock no longer held during build, so concurrent cache misses for the same NamespacedResource each run a full bleve build (N× CPU, memory, disk I/O; N−1 built indexes discarded, leaking memory or leaving orphaned file-based directories)
matched_golden_ids: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes a cache-stampede/race where cacheMu is not held during the expensive index build, allowing multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same index for the same key, matching the golden issue caused by narrowing the lock to only the final cache assignment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent bleve.New(dir, ...) calls on the same directory path can fail or corrupt the on-disk index

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held b.cacheMu for the entire method (including bleve.New(dir, mapper)), serializing concurrent index creation. The diff removes that broad lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This allows two goroutines to call BuildIndex concurrently with the same `key` (thus same `dir := filepath.Join(... key.Namespace ... key.Resource ... key.Group)` when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`) and both execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` simultaneously on the same on-disk path. The diff therefore introduces/exposes the possibility of concurrent on-disk index creation for the same directory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Lazy Init removed — NewResourceServer now calls Init synchronously, changing error contract to constructor error and blocking startup, with no tests verifying failing-init rejection, previously-lazy paths, or alternate construction paths skipping init

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove lazy init: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on init failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go), and all per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls in `Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/...` were removed. This is a meaningful contract/behavior change (constructor can now block/fail) and the diff does not add tests covering init-failure at construction time or the previous lazy-init paths; only a test skip was added elsewhere.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Integration test TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer silently skipped for postgres with a 'works locally' TODO, removing coverage for a major backend in a lifecycle-changing PR

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a new conditional skip for postgres in `TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer` with a TODO comment: `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }`. This removes integration test coverage for the postgres backend, which is a concrete, diff-grounded review concern but not a product/runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Narrowed mutex scope in bleveBackend.BuildIndex allows concurrent duplicate index builds for the same key racing to write cache and clobbering the same directory, with no concurrency test

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, bleveBackend.BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire method (covering cache check + potential bleve.New(dir, ...) / build). The diff removes that broad lock and now only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx`. This permits two goroutines calling BuildIndex concurrently for the same `key` to both observe a cache miss and both proceed to create/build an index (including writing to the same on-disk `dir := filepath.Join(...)` when `size > b.opts.FileThreshold`). That can lead to duplicate work, cache clobbering (last writer wins), and potential filesystem/index corruption or errors from concurrent creation in the same directory. The diff does not add any other per-key synchronization or a concurrency test to cover this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Init ordering change (search.init before initWatcher) untested — no test asserts no events are handled before index build or that events during build aren't lost

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly changes init ordering in `server.Init`: it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (previously watcher started first). This is a nontrivial behavioral change affecting whether events can be received/processed while the search index is still building. The diff contains no corresponding tests or assertions around event handling during initialization (the only test change is skipping postgres in an unrelated integration test), so the review concern about the ordering change being untested is specific and grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Tracer.Start calls changed from dropping ctx to propagating it (child spans now inherit context), but no test verifies span parentage to prevent regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show several `tracer.Start` calls changed from `_, span := ...` to `ctx, span := ...` (e.g., `pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go` and `pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go`), but the finding’s core claim—“no test verifies span parentage to prevent regression”—is not verifiable from this diff alone. The diff doesn’t touch tracing tests, but that does not prove such tests don’t exist elsewhere in the repo.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P1: Event-loss window — moving initWatcher() after search.init() means events written between the snapshot RV and watcher start can be missed, leaving a silently stale search index (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~300-308)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change init ordering in server.Init(): it now runs `s.search.init(ctx)` before `s.initWatcher()` (moved block around ~300). That could create a gap if search.init builds a snapshot and relies on the watcher to catch concurrent writes, but the diff does not show how `search.init` snapshots/records an RV or how the watcher/event stream behaves. Also, Init is now called eagerly in `NewResourceServer` before the server is returned, which may reduce the likelihood of concurrent writes during init. So the claimed event-loss/stale-index defect is plausible but not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Shrinking the cacheMu critical section in BuildIndex allows concurrent bleve.New calls on the same directory, causing spurious errors or divergent index instances (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:~85-138)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, BuildIndex previously held cacheMu for the entire method, preventing concurrent builds. The diff removes that lock and only locks around `b.cache[key] = idx` at the end. This permits two goroutines to concurrently execute `bleve.New(dir, mapper)` / `bleve.NewMemOnly(mapper)` for the same `key` (and same `dir` on disk), potentially creating competing index instances and leading to spurious errors from the backend or last-writer-wins overwrites in the cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Nil-pointer panic in History/Origin when search is not configured — they call s.search.History/Origin without a nil guard, unlike Search (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~922-930)

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go, Search() explicitly guards `if s.search == nil { return nil, fmt.Errorf("search index not configured") }`, but History() and Origin() directly call `return s.search.History(ctx, req)` / `return s.search.Origin(ctx, req)` with no nil check. Since Init() only initializes search when `s.search != nil` and does not error when it’s nil, a server without search configured can reach these methods and panic on a nil pointer dereference.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Watcher/search goroutines inherit the constructor-only ctx, so if the constructor's ctx is cancelled after construction, background work silently dies with no lazy-init fallback (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:~255-261)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows NewResourceServer now eagerly calls `s.Init(ctx)` during construction (server.go ~255+) and removes the per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` calls from methods like Create/Update/Watch/Search/etc. This means initialization (including `s.search.init(ctx)` which now propagates the started tracing context) is tied to whatever `ctx` is available at construction time, with no later “lazy init” using request contexts. The claim that background goroutines will "silently die" on constructor ctx cancellation isn’t directly verifiable from the shown diff (e.g., `initWatcher()` takes no ctx and we can’t see whether `search.init`’s goroutine uses `ctx.Done()`), but the architectural concern about coupling init to a constructor-scoped ctx and removing the fallback is real and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: Integration test for this server is unconditionally skipped on postgres with a TODO, silently reducing CI coverage and possibly masking a real regression (pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38)

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly adds a conditional skip for postgres in TestIntegrationWillRunInstrumentationServerWhenTargetHasNoHttpServer (pkg/server/module_server_test.go) with a TODO comment: `if dbType == "postgres" { t.Skip("skipping - test not working with postgres in Drone. Works locally.") }`. This reduces CI coverage for postgres and could mask regressions, but it is not a product correctness defect in runtime code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: Startup now blocks and fails hard on a full index build since Init moved into NewResourceServer, converting degraded-but-working startup into hard failure for large installs (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:255-261)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does move initialization into construction: `NewResourceServer` now calls `s.Init(ctx)` and returns an error on failure (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go added block around lines ~255-261), while the per-RPC `Init` calls were removed from nearly all handlers (Create/Update/Delete/Read/List/Watch/Search/etc). Since `Init` includes `s.search.init(ctx)` (which can be expensive/blocking) and can fail, this change can shift that cost/failure from “on first request” to “during server creation/startup”, potentially causing startup to block or fail earlier. However, the claim that this converts a previously “degraded-but-working startup” into failure is not fully supported by the diff because previously every RPC path also called `Init` and would return the init error anyway, so the server wouldn’t be functionally usable once invoked.
